cohort: Primigravid teenage girls aged 19 years or younger and adult women aged 20-29 years with singleton term normal pregnancies who delivered at Hail Maternity Hospital during January 1 - December 31, 2013
finding: The study found that teenage pregnancy was associated with a higher risk of low birthweight, while adult mothers experienced more cesarean section and vacuum extraction deliveries.
mod_finding: Adult mothers experienced a higher incidence of cesarean section and vacuum extraction compared to teenage mothers.
